assumptions.description: Use the 18 selected source marginal items as equal-weight descriptive population scenarios. Source weights and SD divisors are unknown; published individual SDs anchor marginal dispersion, never conditional residual SD or estimator precision. A prospective ddof=1 output diagnostic is an approximation, not the original estimator. Source imputed age/BMI and MIND mean/mode filling may alter these margins and dependence. No missingness mechanism is reconstructed.

Conditional on sex, three independent standard normals construct ZA, ZB=-0.15 ZA+sqrt(1-0.15^2) EB, and ZG=0.20 ZA+bS ZB+sqrt(1-0.20^2-bS^2-2*0.20*bS*(-0.15)) EG, with bM=0.30 and bF=0.40. The sign, magnitude, sex interaction, Gaussian tails and all conditional independences are scientific assumptions, unsupported by the admitted marginal evidence. These moderate loadings describe one scenario of age/adiposity/glucose association, not causal coefficients or a required target pattern.

Each context has a declared female probability p. Randomized rounding of 5000*p and random permutation create a stratified sex composition with both categories. For each latent variable Y=Z+d*S, apply F(Y)=(1-p)*Phi(Y)+p*Phi(Y-d) before the marginal inverse CDF. This retains the declared unconditional marginal distribution while introducing sex dependence. Sex rank shifts are explicit assumptions: MIND age/BMI/glucose=(0.10,0.35,-0.08), Ayele=(0.10,0.40,-0.08), target=(0.12,0.60,-0.08). Finite sex rounding introduces at most 1/5000 composition error; no moments or coefficients are tuned on the realized sample.

MIND Table1 age 69.5 (SD 4.2), BMI 25.0 (SD 3.6), FSG 5.2 (SD 1.4), and female 2049/3547 define this source scenario. Age uses a bounded beta on [61,80]; BMI and FSG use lognormal margins. The baseline FSG distribution already includes whatever residual, treatment and laboratory variation contributed to the published selected-source summary; no extra instrument noise or feeding excursion is added. Demographics/BMI were collected in 2018 and glucose in April-May 2019; no age transformation is made. Follow-up fitness, dementia/disability exclusions, history/laboratory completeness, unknown imputation counts and nonrepresentative rural selection remain source-specific limitations, not target eligibility.

For Ayele, use imputed counts 371/187/121/193 out of 872 in [25,35), [35,45), [45,55), [55,64], choosing Methods ages 25-64 over the discrepant 25-65 table captions. Three arbitrary within-bin beta prototypes (all Beta(1,9), all Beta(9,1), and Beta(1,19) in the first two bins/Beta(19,1) in the last two) span differing within-bin spread. A finite 3x3 linear moment equation derives their common mixture weights from reported mean 40.4 and individual SD 13. The prototypes are a nonunique smooth completion of the margins, not recovered individual ages. This high within-bin uncertainty and possible mean/SD/category weighting incompatibility remain limitations.

Ayele BMI probabilities use reported imputed counts 65/467/340 divided once by 872, not rounded printed percentages. Within underweight and normal categories use scaled Beta(2,2) on (12,18.5) and (18.5,24.9); above 25 use 25+Gamma(shape=2,scale=3). These within-category shapes and the lower bound 12 are assumptions. Zero mass in (24.9,25) explicitly completes the literal source categories, not a claim of a biological gap or a recoding of their endpoints. The tail and all within-category associations are unsupported.

No target composition or outcomes are supplied. Target age is 40+Gamma(shape=2,scale=10) with no upper truncation; female probability is 0.56; BMI is lognormal with arithmetic mean 26 and SD 5.5. Basal recorded-scale glucose uses mean 5.3 and SD 1.7, a deliberately broader, slightly shifted assumption relative to the selected MIND anchor. These values are fixed scenario choices, not estimates of HAALSI. Source restrictions, field imputation, sample sizes or original age timing do not become target restrictions; target age retains its supplied census-date interpretation.

MIND is represented directly on its reported serum FSG scale. Ayele has no admitted continuous glucose margin: its basal mean 5.1 and SD 1.5 and all glucose relationships are assumed. For Ayele, three repeated days share basal glucose and have independent feeding indicators (probability 0.45), gamma meal increments (mean 0.9, SD 0.7 mmol/L), and multiplicative device variation (mean multiplier 1, CV 0.06), then average. Target uses one pooled reading, feeding probability 0.50, the same assumed meal increment distribution, and instrument multiplier mean 1.02/CV 0.06. The target 1.02 is an unvalidated measurement sensitivity choice, not an assay conversion. Feeding is conditionally independent of age/sex/BMI/basal glucose and across repeated days; treatment and stable disease heterogeneity remain in the baseline distribution. Exact feeding proportions, model-specific calibration, adherence, treatment composition, and true between-day dependence are unknown. Shared mmol/L does not establish equivalence to serum or source repeated capillary readings.

Positive BMI/glucose margins use lognormal arithmetic moment identities sigma^2=log(1+(s/m)^2) and mu=log(m)-sigma^2/2, producing heteroscedastic absolute-scale residuals and an unbounded upper tail. The marginal SD includes all modeled covariate associations and does not become their conditional residual SD. Gamma meal shape=(mean/SD)^2 and scale=SD^2/mean. These families exclude an explicit diabetes/treatment class, diagnostic thresholds and clinical diagnoses; no OR-to-slope or prevalence-to-tail translation is attempted.

This is one fixed structural/transport scenario. Random seeds represent individual variation and Monte Carlo error, not evidence, parameter or transport uncertainty. Sources remain distinct cohorts; repeated records from one cohort are not independent confirmations. Named geographies support separation but record-level nonoverlap is unverified. Ayele adjusted ORs concern composite diabetes and different adjustment variables, not continuous glucose; Bahendeka abstract-only weighted results remain contextual and unused numerically. All three requested OLS projections are assumption-dependent and unvalidated; source agreement cannot validate target signs, interactions, causal effects, prevalence or clinical use.

Target output represents continuous positive released-cleaned POC values without inventing unknown masses at substitution/boundary readings, device limits or missingness flags. No fasting, treatment, tail or disability exclusions are applied to the target. The unavailable cleaning map and latent-versus-recorded distinction limit target use. Probability subtraction may be clipped to [0,1] solely inside source category interpolation; the target uses paired CDF/survival inversion with no clinical-value trimming or age upper cutoff. A failing table is rejected whole.

Population and measurement descriptor strings are copied mechanically from supplied source templates and target descriptor. Every scheduled context has 5000 rows and identical ordered columns id,age,sex,bmi,glucose in units 1,year,1,kg/m^2,mmol/L. Context selection changes only active_context in the same specification. Exact eligibility is target age>=40, MIND 61-80, Ayele 25-64, with F/M, unique string IDs and finite positive BMI/glucose. No target data or external source has been inspected.

active_context.derivation: Copy target_descriptor.id as initial active context. Only this selector changes mechanically between contexts.

contexts.derivation: Route=inline_deterministic. Descriptors are exact template/target copies; source n_rows=task.n_rows. MIND moments come from Table1 total mean(SD), female ratio 2049/3547 already unit1. Ayele means and sex/age counts come from Table1, BMI counts from Table2; use imputed columns and denominator872, preserving printed percentages separately. MIND beta: t=(69.5-61)/(80-61), v=(4.2/(80-61))^2, k=t(1-t)/v-1, alpha=t*k,beta=(1-t)*k. Ayele p_j=count_j/872; for prototype h and bin j let f_hj=alpha/(alpha+beta), v_hj=alpha*beta/((alpha+beta)^2*(alpha+beta+1)), m_hj=L_j+w_j*f_hj; M_h=sum p_j*m_hj; Q_h=sum p_j*(m_hj^2+w_j^2*v_hj). Solve the fixed 3x3 system with columns (1,M_h,Q_h) and RHS (1,40.4,40.4^2+13^2) for prototype probabilities before sampling; reject invalid probabilities. This is algebraic moment completion, not optimization or source-model fitting on host. Ayele category probabilities are count/872. Lognormal transforms use sigma^2=log1p((SD/mean)^2), mu=log(mean)-sigma^2/2. Gamma meal shape=(0.9/0.7)^2 and scale=0.7^2/0.9. Instrument log variance=log1p(CV^2), log location=log(multiplier)-logvariance/2. Target and Ayele glucose values not reported are fixed assumptions. Mean/SD identities are distribution-level approximations under A01, not assertions of exact finite-sample matching or verified original weighting.

joint_copula.derivation: Fixed assumed loadings. Each sex-specific ZG has conditional variance a^2+bS^2+2*a*bS*rho+residual_variance=1. Apply sex-location-mixture PIT F(z+d*S)=(1-p)Phi(z+d*S)+pPhi(z+d*S-d), then chosen marginal quantiles. The female BMI loading differs from the male loading; requested absolute-scale adjusted OLS effects emerge from this nonlinear joint distribution and measurement process, and are not input coefficients.

sampling.derivation: nF=floor(n*p+U), followed by random sex-label permutation. Conditional latent normals and repeat-level random effects use numpy default_rng(seed). All parameter derivations precede the first random draw. No sample recentering, rescaling, rejection sampling, optimization, row filtering or trial execution is performed.
